senses.definition: A type, race or category; a group of entities that have common characteristics such that they may be grouped together.
examples: What kind of (a) person are you?
This is a strange kind of tobacco.
What kind of ice-cream would you like? There's chocolate, strawberry, and lemon.

quotes.text: How diversely Love doth his pageants play, / And shews his powre in variable kinds !

“[…] the awfully hearty sort of Christmas cards that people do send to other people that they don't know at all well. You know. The kind that have mottoes like
 Here's rattling good luck and roaring good cheer, / With lashings of food and great hogsheads of beer. […]”

quotes.text: That in virtue of which all of his material parts are of the same kind human being is what makes those parts belong to Hook, but Hook is neither identical with his kind (the essence of human being), nor is Hook merely that which makes him a member of the kind or all his parts human (his soul).

senses.definition: A makeshift or otherwise atypical specimen.
examples: The opening served as a kind of window.

quotes.text: I got my traps out of the canoe and made me a nice camp in the thick woods. I made a kind of a tent out of my blankets to put my things under so the rain couldn't get at them.

senses.definition: (archaic) One's inherent nature; character, natural disposition.

quotes.text: Must yt nedes folowe that theyr fayth was chaunged in kynde, bycause yt was augmented in degrees.
quotes.reference: 1533, Thomas More, The second parte of the confutacion of Tyndals answere in whyche is also confuted the chyrche that Tyndale deuyseth:

quotes.text: The generall woorde, is spoken of many, that differ either in kynd, or els in nombre.
quotes.reference: 1551, Thomas Wilson, The rule of reason, conteinyng the arte of logique:

quotes.text: 'Tis all one..whether our Afflictions be the same with those of others, in Kind, or not Superiour to them in Degree.
quotes.reference: 1665, Robert Boyle, Occasional Reflections upon Several Subjects. Whereto is premis'd a Discourse about such kind of thoughts:

quotes.text: He also argued powerfully, if less influentially, that animals' and humans' capacities differ largely in degree and not in kind.

examples:
My young love said to me, My mother won’t mind
And my father won’t slight you for your lack of kind.

senses.definition: Goods or services used as payment, as e.g. in barter.
examples: I don't have any money but I can pay in kind by washing the dishes.

quotes.text: Some of you, on pure instinct of nature, / Are led by kind t'admire your fellow-creature.
quotes.reference: 1691, John Dryden, Prologue to King Arthur:

senses.definition: Equivalent means used as response to an action.
examples: I'll pay in kind for his insult.

senses.definition: (Christianity) Each of the two elements of the communion service, bread and wine.
(type theory) The type of a type constructor or a higher-order type operator.
examples: The kind of any primitive data type is *, corresponding to a nullary constructor.

senses.definition: Having a benevolent, courteous, friendly, generous, gentle, liberal, sympathetic, or warm-hearted nature or disposition, marked by consideration for – and service to – others.
